“Whatever you do, Mole, don’t fuss,” said the Rat, pushing the boat from the bank with a practiced thrust. “It’s a perfectly simple matter, and the day is much too fine to be wasted on worry.” The Mole leaned back against the cushions, trailing one paw in the water, and watched the reeds slide by. He had never in his life been on the river, and every turn showed him something new: a moorhen darting for cover, a field of buttercups, a distant mill with its wheel turning lazily. “I do believe,” he said, with deep contentment, “that this is the finest way of spending a morning that I ever heard of.” The Rat only smiled, and rowed on.
